questions.q: Your picture looks the same with and without the LoRA, and the log shows 'lora key not loaded' for every key. What does that mean?
options: The file was made for another model family, so nothing matched
questions.answer: The file was made for another model family, so nothing matched
questions.why: Row 4 of the lab: no key in the file found a weight in the model, so there are zero patches.

questions.q: You load a LoRA with LoraLoaderModelOnly and see warnings for lora_te keys only. What should you do?
options: Nothing, if you meant to skip the text encoder: the denoiser keys loaded
questions.answer: Nothing, if you meant to skip the text encoder: the denoiser keys loaded
questions.why: The model-only loader passes clip None, so text-encoder keys aren't in the key map and get warned about.

questions.q: With LoraLoader, your prompt nodes are wired to the checkpoint's CLIP. What is the effect of strength_clip?
options: It does nothing to your prompt
questions.answer: It does nothing to your prompt
questions.why: The patch is on the CLIP the loader outputs. A prompt encoded through the other CLIP never sees it.

questions.q: You chain two LoRAs at 0.8 and 0.5. What do you get?
options: Both changes added to the weight, in either order, up to rounding
The first, then the second replacing it
questions.answer: Both changes added to the weight, in either order, up to rounding
questions.why: Each loader appends a patch to the list, and each patch adds to the weight.

questions.q: Two files hold the same up and down numbers at rank 4. One has alpha 4 and the other has alpha 1. At strength 1 how do they compare?
options: The first changes the weight four times as much
The second changes the weight four times as much
questions.answer: The first changes the weight four times as much
questions.why: The scale is alpha / rank, so 1.0 against 0.25. The lab measures 0.6564 against 0.1641.
